On this page

The standard and its implementations ​

Mosaic is three different things kept in one repository. They change at different speeds and promise different things:

LayerWhat it isWhere it livesWhat it promises
The standardThe shape of a Mosaic file and of the HTTP API, as JSON Schema and OpenAPIstandard/, generated from src/What any reader or writer, in any language, can rely on
The reference implementationThe TypeScript SDK, the IFC converter and the viewersdk/ts, sdk/ifc4One working reading of the standard, plus conventions built on top of it
The CLIThe mosaic commandsdk/cliA thin wrapper exposing the reference implementation as commands
src/*.tsp ──tsp compile──▶ standard/*.json ──quicktype──▶ sdk/ts (types)
                                                          │
                                       sdk/ts + sdk/ifc4 ─┴─▶ sdk/cli  (mosaic …)
                                                          └─▶ viewer

The arrows only go one way. The standard does not know the SDK exists. The SDK's types are generated from the standard, and the CLI adds no behaviour of its own: every command calls a function in the SDK that you can also call from your own code.

Pre-1.0

All three layers are still moving, the standard included. Its version string (MosaicVersion) is currently "post-alpha".

Why the split matters ​

If you are writing another implementation, in C#, Python or Rust, the standard is the contract. Validate against mosaic-index-file.schema.json and you can read and write Mosaic without any of the TypeScript code.

If you are using Mosaic from TypeScript, the SDK gives you a lot more than the standard does: packing, federating, selecting, composing to glTF, converters and a database. Most of that is behaviour the schemas do not define, so another implementation may not do it, or may do it differently.

If you only want the tools, the CLI is all you need. It ships as a single executable, and everything it does is described in The CLI section of these docs.

Generating the standard ​

bash
cd src
npm install
npm run compile-json-spec

The TypeSpec compiler reads mosaic-json-file.tsp and writes standard/mosaic-index-file.schema.json, as configured in tspconfig.yaml. Commit the regenerated output alongside the spec change. The API standard is generated the same way, with npm run compile-api-spec.

In this section ​

  • File standard: the index file schema, field by field, and how it is generated. The format, by example opens up a real archive.
  • API standard: the OpenAPI description of the HTTP API.

The reference implementation is described in The SDK and The CLI: what they build on top of the standard, and where they currently fall short of it.
